images.filename: Edward Hyatt Powerplant during its shutdown in August 2021-5993.jpg
images.caption: Edward Hyatt Powerplant at Oroville Dam on August 15, 2021. In early August 2021, the hydroelectric power plant was shut down due to low water levels in Lake Oroville caused by the drought in California. The powerplant is the fourth-largest hydroelectric energy producer statewide and had to be shut down for the first time since it opened in 1967.
images.alt: Edward Hyatt Powerplant at Oroville Dam on August 15, 2021. In early August 2021, the hydroelectric power plant was shut down due to low water levels in Lake Oroville caused by the drought in California. The powerplant is the fourth-largest hydroelectric energy producer statewide and had to be shut down for the first time since it opened in 1967.

images.filename: Oroville Dam main spillway 30 March 2011.jpg
images.caption:
(Original Caption) The California Department of Water Resources released water from the Oroville Dam spillway into the Feather River to make way for the expected higher than normal spring and summer runoff. Oroville Lake was at 106 percent of average for the date in late March, with a 81 percent of its 3.5 million acre-foot capacity. Photo taken March 30, 2011. 
Paul Hames / California Department of Water Resources
images.alt:
(Original Caption) The California Department of Water Resources released water from the Oroville Dam spillway into the Feather River to make way for the expected higher than normal spring and summer runoff. Oroville Lake was at 106 percent of average for the date in late March, with a 81 percent of its 3.5 million acre-foot capacity. Photo taken March 30, 2011. 
Paul Hames / California Department of Water Resources
